ashby:abby-care:ba7fbc4f-ed31-47c6-8679-.summary:
Abby Care is building the leading AI-native platform for family-led care. America is facing a growing care crisis. Millions more people need care at home than ever. Over 50 million family caregivers support loved ones without the tools, training, or recognition they deserve.

We believe families are the largest untapped caregiving workforce in America, and that technology can help them deliver better care while driving stronger outcomes and greater transparency across the healthcare system.

Abby Care combines clinical oversight with an AI-powered platform to train, enable, and support family caregivers in delivering high-quality care at home. Our platform helps health plans and government partners better understand, verify, and improve care in the home. We expand access to care, reduce reliance on higher-cost settings, and help ensure public dollars are spent effectively.

We are proud…

sections.title: The Opportunity:
paras:
As a Staff Product Manager , you’ll set the standard for how every AI-powered feature in Abby’s platform reaches a caregiver or a clinician. You’ll operate across Abby’s core products (caregiver and clinician) making sure the signal a caregiver captures contributes to the judgement a clinician acts on.

Part of your responsibility is to ensure AI features are ready to leave shadow mode and to ensure that the AI portfolio is trustworthy, coherent, and shipped with rigor. At the Staff level, you are expected to be a force multiplier: operating with high autonomy,, closely partnering closely with our founder, clinical, and engineering leadership to redefine what is possible in home-based care, and influencing how the entire product organization thinks about AI.

This is a Full-Time Hybrid opportunity based in San Francisco.

sections.title: What you’ll work on:
bullets: Define the Evaluation Standard: Own the gate clinical or caregiver-facing AI features have to clear. Decide what “ready” means and raise the bar for features to get there.

Own Cross-Surface AI Consistency: A patient’s baseline, care plan, and chart notes are read and written by both the caregiver and clinician products. Ensure that those systems reason about the same patient the same way, so a signal captured on one surface is reflected in the other.

Set the Bar for AI Product Development: : Partner closely with the PMs on other product areas to raise the standard of their AI-feature specs, their evaluation criteria, and their partnership with Applied AI.
Partner Directly with Applied AI Leadership: Work at the architecture level on how caregiver AI and clinician AI are evaluated, monitored, and iterated post-launch.

Build for Regulated, Clinically Critical Ground Truth: Ensure that evaluation frameworks hold up against clinical scrutiny and payer/compliance review. Partner with clinical leadership and compliance to make sure that products measured against clinician dispositions are rigorous enough to trust.

sections.title: What success looks like:
bullets: Clinical or caregiver-facing AI features that reach production clear a documented shadow-mode evaluation against real dispositions.
Caregiver-side and clinician-side AI systems can be proven to reason consistently about the same patient with no contradicting baselines or signals that are dropped at the handoff between surfaces.
Other AI PMs at Abby Care treat your evaluation standard as the bar.

sections.title: What you’ll have:
bullets: Experience: 8+ years of product management experience, with a proven track record of leading complex, high-impact AI or ML product initiatives at a Staff or Lead PM level in a high-growth tech environment.

AI Product Depth: Direct experience designing evaluation frameworks for AI systems in production and deciding how AI features’ real-world performance is measured, monitored, and gated before and after launch.

Technical Fluency: Strong technical acumen, particularly in working with engineering and Applied ML and AI teams to build data-intensive or AI-driven platforms. You don't need to write code, but you must be able to deeply evaluate technical trade-offs.
Customer Obsession: Deep empathy for users (in our case, family caregivers and care recipients) and a rigorous approach to qualitative and quantitative research in a regulated environment.
Relentless Resourcefulness: You thrive in fast-paced startup environments. You adapt quickly, solve challenges with creativity, and deliver results without unnecessary complexity.
Exceptional Communication: The ability to distill complex healthcare and technical concepts into clear, actionable product requirements and compelling strategic narratives for executive stakeholders.

ashby:betterup:5d56e8ee-9d91-44a9-b09e-2.summary:
Let's face it, a company whose mission is human transformation better have some fresh thinking about the employer/employee relationship.

We do. We can't cram it all in here, but you'll start noticing it from the first interview.

Even our candidate experience is different. And when you get an offer from us (and accept it), you get way more than a paycheck. You get a personal BetterUp Coach, a development plan, a trained and coached manager, the most amazing team you've ever met (yes, each with their own personal BetterUp Coach), and most importantly, work that matters.

This makes for a remarkably focused and fulfilling work experience. Frankly, it's not for everyone. But for people with fire in their belly, it's a game-changing, career-defining, soul-lifting move.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: Our largest customers no longer decide on the demo. They decide on what happens after: whether their HR systems connect, whether provisioning works, whether coaching shows up inside the tools their people already have open, whether our AI behaves the way their risk team needs it to. Forward Deployment is the function that owns that work.

This role takes the accounts nobody has solved. One is an eight-figure decision waiting on a commercial model that doesn't exist yet. On another, the champion left, the last co-creation attempt damaged trust, and we have never been able to see their usage data. On a third, an executive told us the platform is strategic and 2% of the seats have been assigned.

On those accounts there is no charter to execute. You write it. That means deciding what technical success even means here, what we'll commit to, what we'll refuse, and whether a squad belongs on this account at all. Some of these problems are commercial or political rather than technical, and part of the job is recognizing that early, saying so plainly, and not spending engineers on it.

sections.title: What You Own
bullets: Define what technical success means on the hardest accounts in the book. You walk in without a baseline, sometimes without instrumentation and sometimes without trust, and you leave with a written charter, named gates, and a customer who believes the next thing we say.

Commit in writing, in both directions. You say what the squad will build and by when, and you say what has to be true on their side for it to matter. You are equally clear about what we will not build.

Carry the relationship at the altitude where the decision actually sits. You'll work a CIO, a CHRO, a procurement lead, and a security architect in the same week, and you'll be the person our own executives put in front of a customer when the account is in trouble.

Clear the technical gates on the account's next commercial decision. The account executive owns the number. You own the gates sitting on its critical path, and you're measured on gates cleared and on influence the deal team confirms in writing. You carry no quota, and nothing about this role changes that.

Lead a squad of two to three forward deployed engineers, and set the standard the rest of the function calibrates to. You won't manage people. The way you write a charter, run a discovery cadence, and close out an engagement becomes how the other squads do it.

Close every engagement in writing. It graduates into the platform with core engineering's acceptance, it converts to paid or drawdown-funded work, or you kill it. You take those decisions to a monthly graduation board and make the case for the ones worth paving into the platform.

Build the prototypes yourself. Use Claude, Cursor, Replit, and Figma Make to put something real in front of a customer before engineering spends a sprint on it. Adjust prompts, change a flow, and run your own data analysis without filing a ticket.

Own the evidence and the argument it supports. Activation and utilization deltas per account, influence claims the deal team confirms, and the pattern across accounts that tells the product organization what the platform should own and what it should stop building.

sections.title: What You'll Bring
bullets: 9+ years in product management, solutions architecture, or a forward deployed role, including several years owning the technical relationship on enterprise accounts where the contract value ran into seven or eight figures.
A record of turning around an account that was going badly: trust damaged, a previous attempt failed, or a competitor already in the building.

Enterprise deployment experience and the scars that come with it. You've shipped against someone else's HRIS, argued your way through a security questionnaire, waited on procurement, and watched a rollout stall because 40% of the licenses were never assigned.

Enough technical depth to be useful. You don't need to write production code, but you should read an API doc without help, reason about a data pipeline, configure an LLM's context and guardrails yourself, and tell an engineer when an approach won't survive the customer's security review.
Credibility with executives on both sides of the table. You've briefed a customer's leadership team and your own, and you've delivered bad news to both without losing the room.
Experience in B2B2C, where you sell to an enterprise buyer and build for the people that buyer serves. The two want different things and you've had to hold both.
Domain expertise in organizational transformation, human transformation, or talent intelligence is a plus.

sections.title: Skills & Competencies
bullets: Relentless agency. When something isn't working, you own it and fix it instead of naming the team that should have. Humility about what you don't know, and relentlessness about figuring it out anyway.

The discipline to say no. A happy customer asking for one more thing is the hardest no in this job, and so is telling your own leadership that an account they care about isn't a Forward Deployment problem. You can do both without damaging the relationship.

Judgment about what generalizes. You can tell the difference between a custom build worth paving into the platform and one customer's snowflake, and you'll argue for the distinction in front of core engineering.

Executive communication. You can walk into a quarterly business review and tell the story of what you shipped, what it moved, and what you got wrong, to an audience that includes both a CIO and a talent leader.
AI-native fluency. Prototyping with agents is your default operating method, not a novelty you bring out for demos.
Comfort deciding on incomplete information. You listen, synthesize, decide, and move. When you're wrong you correct fast and say so. You don't stall waiting for consensus.

ashby:dave:264e5d99-07bd-4966-80c9-49166.summary: Dave is a financial app on a mission to build products that level the financial playing field. It is redefining the financial landscape by leveraging technology to create an affordable, transparent, and user-centric access to liquidity for millions of Americans. As a leading innovator in the U.S. financial services sector, Dave’s digital financial platform offers products designed to meet the credit needs of those underserved by traditional financial institutions. Dave’s offerings include its flagship ExtraCash product, providing members up to $500 within minutes. The company is on track to launch several new product offerings in 2026, including a Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) option.

sections.title: Dave vs. Goliath. We’re Dave.
paras: Dave is focused on serving Americans who are financially vulnerable or living paycheck to paycheck. Dave is leading the charge in creating a new era of credit products that prioritizes speed, affordability, and accessibility, making it the go-to financial partner for those who need it most.

Flex card is Dave's newest and most ambitious product, a pay-in-4 card built for the millions of members living paycheck to paycheck who've never had fair access to credit. Behind every purchase it makes is the system that turns a balance into a loan, casts it into installments, services it, and collects it. That system is the loan management system (LMS), and it's what this role owns.

This is a senior individual-contributor role at the foundation of Flex and every loan product that comes after it. You'll own the LMS and the systems of record end-to-end: the ledger, loan casting, servicing, collections, and the compliance tooling around them. And you'll take it from a single-product build to a scalable platform, so that when Dave launches its next loan product, it runs on what you've built instead of starting over.

sections.title: What You'll Build & Own
bullets: Own the loan management system : Lead the LMS and core systems of record: the ledger, loan casting at billing, the pay-in-4 installment structure, participation and installment fees, repayment, and collections.
Ship the mechanics members feel : installment schedules aligned to paycheck dates, early payoff, and decline and failure handling.
Own the numbers : Define and track system health, payoff rates, and loss performance, and use them to prioritize where to invest.

Enable flawless execution : Work closely with Risk, Legal/Compliance (LECO), Data Science, Engineering, and Operations, and coordinate external partners (Coastal, LoanPro) on anything that touches casting, collections, or compliance.

sections.title: The Impact
paras: The LMS is where Flex's unit economics are won or lost. Payoff rates, loss performance, and whether members can repay on a schedule that fits their paycheck all run through the system you'll own and small improvements compound across every loan.

You'll be building this foundation at its most formative stage. Get it right and Dave launches its next loan product in a fraction of the time, on infrastructure that's already compliant, auditable, and proven. The problems are real, the stakes are high, and your fingerprints will be all over how Dave lends for years to come.

Direct experience across the lending lifecycle (origination, underwriting, servicing, repayment, collections) and the risk and compliance considerations throughout

Comfort setting direction in ambiguous, greenfield areas and driving execution across functions without formal authority
Strong analytical skills; comfortable using data to inform decisions
Proven ability to use AI tools as a force multiplier for speed, quality, and impact

Who You Are

You code. Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or both. You've built and shipped things that went beyond the spec.

We started Loancrate to make home-buying simpler and less expensive for lenders and borrowers. Today, mortgage lenders are stuck running their companies on software products built 20 years ago. These products are slow, unstable, and don't lead to material improvements in efficiency. When using these systems, the average human cost to originate a loan is still over $11,000.

Loancrate builds AI-native tooling to automate mortgage workflows. Our ultimate goal is fully automated origination, which has the potential to save lenders over $16B in operating expense per year.

Since starting in 2020, our remote team has enabled our customers to power >$85 billion in new home loans. We care about collaboration, very open communication covering the good & the bad so that we learn from our decisions quickly, and ultimately having fun while we're building. You'll fit in well if you like diving deep…

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: Buying a new loan origination system is the easy part. Actually configuring it to match how a lender runs its business - their conditions, their disclosures, their underwriting guidelines, their quirks - is where implementations are won or lost. We're looking for an Implementation Consultant to be the person in the room (virtually or on-site) who makes that configuration work actually happen.

This is a forward-deployed, hands-on role. You'll work directly with a lender's team during the implementation phase to configure Loancrate around their workflows, answer their configuration questions, and get them through user acceptance testing. Once the customer is live, you roll off and move to the next implementation - the CSM stays on as the long-term relationship owner, and the Implementation Lead keeps the overall project plan on track, while you're the one actually in the product with the customer making it work.

Because this role sits inside an active mortgage workflow from day one, you need to already be fluent in mortgage - not learning it as you go. We can teach you Loancrate inside and out. What we can't do in any reasonable timeframe is teach you what a lender's processors and underwriters actually need a system to do for them.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Act as the forward-deployed implementation expert - work directly with the customer's team to configure Loancrate around their specific workflows, conditions, and business rules.

Translate a lender's current-system setup into a Loancrate configuration - take how they operate today and recommend (and build) the configuration that gets them the same outcome, or better, in Loancrate.

Own testing support during UAT - respond to configuration and testing questions as they come in, and work the "UAT Blocked" queue in Jira so customer-reported blockers get resolved quickly instead of sitting.
Troubleshoot configuration issues in real time - when something isn't behaving the way the customer expects, you're the one who can dig in, find the root cause, and fix it or escalate it clearly.

Work closely with the Implementation Lead and CSM - you're heads-down on configuration and testing; they're managing the timeline and the broader relationship, and you keep them informed of anything that could affect either.
Roll off cleanly at go-live - document the final configuration and any open items clearly enough that the CSM can pick up the relationship without a gap.
Help build the implementation playbook - common configuration patterns, frequently asked setup questions, and testing checklists that make the next implementation faster than the last.
Willingness to travel - expect approximately once-a-month domestic US travel to customer sites, with occasional additional trips around key milestones like UAT kickoff and go-live.

sections.title: What Success Looks Like
paras: By the 12-18 month mark, you'll have implemented multiple lenders end-to-end, be a go-to resource for tricky configuration scenarios, and be a candidate to help train and ramp future Implementation Consultants as the team grows.
bullets: Be the hands-on configuration owner on at least one active implementation, trusted by the customer to answer setup questions directly.
Have cleared UAT-Blocked tickets at a pace that keeps testing moving rather than stalling on your queue.
Have handled a real configuration curveball - a workflow that doesn't map cleanly to Loancrate - and worked it to a resolution the customer was happy with.
Have a direct working relationship with your Implementation Lead and CSM, with a clear handoff process for when you roll off a project.

sections.title: Required Skills and Background
bullets: Direct mortgage experience - you've worked at a lender or mortgage tech company and understand the origination-to-closing lifecycle (1003, LE, CD, AUS findings, conditions, lock extensions) well enough to configure a system around it without hand-holding.

Hands-on experience with a loan origination system (Encompass, Empower, Byte, or similar) - you've worked inside one, ideally helped configure or administer one, and know where lenders' real-world workflows get tricky.
Comfort working hands-on in software configuration - you're not afraid to get into settings, rules, and workflows yourself rather than just describing what needs to change to someone else.
Testing and troubleshooting instincts - you can read a bug report or a UAT ticket, reproduce the issue, and tell the difference between a configuration fix, a training gap, and an actual product bug.
Clear, patient communication - you'll be answering the same category of question from different customers constantly, and need to do it clearly and without making anyone feel behind.
Comfort with a project-phase role - you're energized by the intensity of an implementation and the clean handoff at the end, rather than wanting to own the long-term relationship.
Bias to action and comfort with ambiguity - we're building this function from the ground up; you'll be figuring out the right way to configure something as often as you're executing a known pattern.
Curiosity about AI and how it's changing mortgage workflows - you don't need an ML background, but you should be excited to help configure and explain AI-driven features to customers.

You're technical enough to own the configuration yourself: you understand APIs, data flows, retrieval and authentication, and you use AI coding tools to extend what Pi does, with the judgement to know when a change makes sense and the discipline to test it before it ships. You're as comfortable running a requirements workshop with a commercial leadership team as you are debugging why Pi made a decision, and you care deeply about the outcome Pi delivers.

More specifically, the people who do this well bring:

sections.title: Competencies
paras: You likely have at least 3 to 4 years of experience, and you're technically competent enough to configure, test and debug an AI agent yourself. That might come from:
More than your title, we care about curiosity, rigour and a bias to action.
bullets: You turn customer requirements into precise Pi configuration: instructions, data, guardrails and escalation paths
You configure and fix things yourself, using AI tools to handle technical changes without waiting on engineering
You test like it matters: you design the scenarios and simulations that define what good looks like, and you don't launch until Pi meets them
You run engagements with energy and structure, keeping customers, timelines and stakeholders moving toward go-live
You own the number: adoption, time saved, revenue retained, whatever the customer deployed Pi to deliver
You are Product's voice from the field, turning what you see across customers into clear, prioritised feedback that makes Pi better
A recent role as a forward-deployed product manager or forward-deployed engineer
Product management on a technical product

sections.title: Trajectory
paras: Pi is Planhat's customer agent: a single agent that can be configured to take on processes across the commercial lifecycle, from onboarding and adoption to renewal and expansion.

Agent Product Managers are the people who make Pi real for each customer. You join once the customer has signed, work directly with them to shape how Pi is configured for their processes, and extend it to new processes and teams. You run a small portfolio of customers, own a specialty commercial area and help shape how the team works.
Everything you learn feeds straight back to Product, so Pi gets better for every customer, and you work closely with Sales, CS, Product and Engineering so no context or momentum is lost.
bullets: Taking Pi live on a customer's renewals process in weeks, from the first requirements session through testing to launch
Setting Pi up to run account management for a customer's long-tail accounts: monitoring health, preparing renewals and handling the outreach no human team has time for
Reviewing a week of Pi's work for a customer, spotting where it falls short, and shipping the fix the same afternoon
Extending Pi from one process to the next for the same customer, until it runs across their commercial lifecycle
Turning a pattern you've seen across five customers into a capability Product builds into Pi for everyone
Run Pi deployments for a portfolio of customers, from kickoff to live and beyond
Agree success metrics with each customer and report on the impact
Help customer leaders decide where Pi goes next

sections.title: Definition of Success
bullets:
Success in this role is measured by what Pi delivers for your customers, and how much better it gets because of you.

• Your customers hit the targets they deployed Pi for
Their leaders come back to you for what's next, and Pi expands into new processes and teams
Product ships improvements to Pi that started with you

ashby:quantexa:09fc86d2-41e2-4c85-a419-0.summary: Do you ever have the urge to do things better than the last time? We do. And it’s this urge that drives us every day. Our environment of discovery and innovation means we’re able to create deep and valuable relationships with our clients to create real change for them and their industries. It’s what got us here – and it’s what will make our future. At Quantexa, you’ll experience autonomy and support in equal measures allowing you to form a career that matches your ambitions. 41% of our colleagues come from an ethnic or religious minority background. We speak over 20 languages across our 50+ nationalities, creating a sense of belonging for all.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: We are looking for an exceptional candidate to join our high-performing Field Engineering Function in Canada – Banking & Public Sector. Reporting into the Director of Field Engineering - Canada, you will collaborate closely with regional peers across Alliances, Sales, Marketing, Product, and Delivery to help win strategic sales opportunities and ensure our customers realise lasting value from the Quantexa platform.

We are seeking someone with strong technical and business solution expertise who can articulate complex technical concepts in a clear, compelling way. You will deliver impactful presentations, product demonstrations, and deep dives across customer engagements and industry events. As a spokesperson for Quantexa's technology, you will build lasting trust with stakeholders by engaging them in relevant, value-driven conversations.

This role is for someone who thrives on ownership and impact. You will work on strategic opportunities and accounts from the first conversation through to successful deployment and expansion, and your insights from the field will help shape how Quantexa evolves.
bullets: Communicate the value and impact of the Quantexa Decision Intelligence Platform, helping prospects understand how it enables smarter, faster, and more confident decision-making through connected, trusted data
Identify and position the right Quantexa solution tailored to each prospect’s and customer’s specific needs
Guide prospects and customers through a clear, outcome-driven solution strategy that sets the stage for long-term value and success
Remain a trusted technical partner beyond the initial sale, supporting successful adoption, business value realisation, and expansion

sections.title: Location
paras: This role will be based in Toronto with hybrid model. To best facilitate collaboration with our customers, partners, and internal teams, this role will involve travel to customer sites across the region and occasional international travel to our other offices, such as London.

sections.title: What You’ll Be Doing
bullets: Be a functional expert in Quantexa’s platform and products, with a strong understanding of its capabilities and real-world applications
Demonstrate a good understanding of the industry practices and regulatory environments of our customers within banking & public sector, and how the platform addresses their challenges
Articulate and present the value of our platform, demonstrating how Quantexa solves specific pain points and enables better decision-making
Represent Quantexa at industry events, customer meetings, and webinars, showcasing our capabilities and thought leadership
Support or manage the technical aspects of the sales cycle, working alongside Sales, Architects, Product, and Domain Subject Matter Experts
Contribute to proposals, including RFPs and RFIs
Take ownership of the design and execution of PoCs and trials, ensuring alignment with customer objectives
Collaborate on the design and iteration of tailored solutions, working with partners, customers, and internal teams to define the right approach

sections.title: What You’ll Bring
bullets: Experience in a commercially focused, technical role such as Solution Engineering, Presales, Technical Sales, Value Consulting, or a customer-facing technical consulting role, working with customers in Banking or Public Sector
Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, with a track record of effective customer engagement
Great communicator, able to captivate audiences of all sizes with an innate ability to simplify complex concepts for diverse audiences.

Proven experience in at least one solution area, such as Data Management, Fraud Detection, Financial Crime, Risk Management, Intelligence Investigations, or National Defense Intelligence, with a good understanding of both technical and business aspects of the solution

Led extensive proving engagement including PoCs or early implementation phases, or alternatively, all of the following activities: technical workshops, prototypes, bespoke demonstrations, and business cases.
A track record of delivering measurable outcomes, such as technical wins, successful deployments, or customer expansion

Experience working with customers beyond the initial sale, for example through platform implementation, adoption, or account management, including helping customers define a roadmap to realise the value of their investment
Ability to build and nurture trusted relationships with senior business and technology stakeholders, up to executive level

ashby:rain:6aa4cf9f-58bd-45a5-bce0-e0da6.summary: Rain is the global stablecoin payments platform for enterprises, neobanks, platforms, developers, and AI agents. Our technology allows partners to move, store, and use stablecoins instantly and compliantly through global payment cards, rewards, on/offramps, wallets, and cross-border rails. As both a Visa and Mastercard Principal Member, Rain issues cards that work at more than 175 million merchant locations in over 220 countries and territories. Built natively for stablecoins and trusted by more than 100 organizations worldwide, Rain delivers secure, scalable infrastructure that makes money move freely and instantly around the world.

sections.title: Our Ethos
paras: We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

sections.title: About the Team
paras: Product Marketing sits within Rain's Marketing & Communications team and owns how we bring Rain's infrastructure to market. The Money Movement line covers onramps, offramps, and payments, the connective tissue between onchain and the world's banking rails. As the world moves onchain, this team's job is to make clear how Rain bridges stablecoins with the rails enterprises already trust, from ACH and SEPA to SWIFT, Fedwire, and local real-time payment schemes. Reporting to our founding PMM, you'll help build the positioning, enablement, and market intelligence that keep Rain ahead as this category matures.

sections.title: What you’ll do
bullets: Own go-to-market for new onramp, offramp, and payments product and feature launches, from positioning through rollout
Build and maintain revenue enablement for both Business Development and post-sales Platform teams, including pitch decks, case studies, and sell sheets, as well as internal training

Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Compliance, and Legal to translate money movement mechanics like liquidity, settlement, FX, and cross-border regulatory nuance into materials teams can act on
Track banking rails and payment schemes around the world, including ACH, SEPA, SWIFT, Fedwire, and regional real-time payment systems, and explain how Rain connects to each
Track competitors in the stablecoin on/offramp space and give internal teams a clear point of view on how Rain wins
Represent the voice of the customer back to Product and Engineering to shape roadmap priorities

sections.title: You are likely to succeed if you have:
bullets: 3-7+ years in product marketing, product management, or sales enablement at a payments company, bank, or money transmitter working directly with cross-border rails and settlement
Deep knowledge of banking rails and payment schemes around the world, including ACH, SEPA, SWIFT, Fedwire, and regional real-time payment systems
A track record selling or marketing payments infrastructure to enterprise-level companies
Genuine interest in how stablecoins and onchain rails are reshaping global money movement
Comfort working cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Compliance, and Legal in a fast-moving environment
Strong writing and communication skills, with the ability to make technical and regulatory complexity clear

ashby:rain:ebb80f27-8c49-439c-8b5f-b3c1b.summary: Rain is the global stablecoin payments platform for enterprises, neobanks, platforms, developers, and AI agents. Our technology allows partners to move, store, and use stablecoins instantly and compliantly through global payment cards, rewards, on/offramps, wallets, and cross-border rails. As both a Visa and Mastercard Principal Member, Rain issues cards that work at more than 175 million merchant locations in over 220 countries and territories. Built natively for stablecoins and trusted by more than 100 organizations worldwide, Rain delivers secure, scalable infrastructure that makes money move freely and instantly around the world.

sections.title: Our Ethos
paras: We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: AI agents are already booking travel, subscribing to software, running procurement end to end, and moving money on behalf of users — much of it through Rain. Our Agent Control Layer is the governing surface for that activity: it enforces approved counterparties, amounts, merchants, and task scope at initiation, before a transaction ever occurs, rather than reconciling damage after the fact.

We are hiring a Senior Product Manager to own that platform. This is a 0-to-1 role inside a category being defined in real time. You will own the developer-facing surface — APIs, SDKs, controls, docs — that teams building agents use to give them spending power safely. McKinsey projects $3–$5 trillion in global agentic commerce by 2030. The primitives that make it trustworthy have not been built yet. You will build them.
You will report to the Head of Product and work daily with engineering, risk and compliance, network partnerships, and the developers shipping on us.

sections.title: What you'll do
paras: • Define the primitives for agent authority: spend scopes, merchant and counterparty allowlists, velocity and amount ceilings, task-bound credentials, human-in-the-loop approvals, and clean revocation.
• Own scoped virtual cards for agents — cards provisioned for a single merchant, amount, and task, retired the moment the task completes.
• Extend the rest of Rain's stack (wallets, virtual accounts, onramps, offramps, cross-border payments) to agent initiators within the parameters our customers define.

sections.title: You’ll likely succeed if you have
paras: • 8+ years in product management, with meaningful time on a developer-facing platform, API, or infrastructure product. You have shipped something engineers chose to build on.

• Technical depth. You read API diffs, write your own queries, prototype against your own endpoints, and hold your own in an architecture review. You don't need to have been an engineer; you do need engineers to take you seriously.
• 0-to-1 instincts. You have taken a product from a blank page to real usage in an ambiguous market, and you're comfortable with a roadmap that changes because the ground moved.

ashby:ramp:d2beca4a-7409-404b-8382-761e5.summary:
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

sections.title: About Ramp
paras: The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Ramp is building institutional partnerships with top global strategy consulting firms that shape finance transformation and technology decisions for the CFOs and CEOs we serve. These firms influence clients before a buying process begins, advise on the operating and technology decisions that define transformation programs, and can help clients move from strategy to live operational capability.

Ramp has an opportunity to build relationships that create value for the firm, its clients, and Ramp, across executive engagement, thought leadership, co-sell, and shared client work. This role will own those relationships and turn them into an institutional go-to-market motion: building credibility with firm leadership, identifying the right client and practice wedges, developing firm-specific plans, leveraging Ramp’s data to amplify firms’ thought leadership, and creating repeatable paths to joint client outcomes.

This is a build from the ground up. Ramp's relationships across this ecosystem are early and largely informal today, and this person will be responsible for the relationship, the partnership thesis, and the operating motion that makes a firm a meaningful Ramp partner over time. It is a broader remit than a typical partnerships role.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own Ramp's relationships with a portfolio of top-tier strategy and advisory firms (e.g., McKinsey, Bain, BCG), serving as the primary relationship owner and building credibility with senior firm leadership
Turn executive introductions into structured partnerships, developing the partnership thesis, relationship map, executive sponsor plan, target practices and client wedge for each firm
Negotiate and close the first formal agreements between Ramp and these firms
Build market-facing proof points with Ramp's leadership, marketing and product teams, including executive events, thought leadership and shared client stories
Coordinate execution across Ramp, bringing the right Account Executives, Customer Success Managers, Product, AI Solutions and executive sponsors into each firm relationship
Establish and maintain the operating cadence: relationship maps, firm plans, account maps and next steps

sections.title: What You Need
bullets: 4+ years of experience at a leading strategy consulting firm (e.g., McKinsey, Bain, BCG)
Exceptional executive presence. You can hold a room with senior leaders, earn trust quickly, and be trusted to represent Ramp in meetings without support
Proven ability to run many work streams and complicated stakeholder management
A builder's instinct. You are energized by an empty page, comfortable without a playbook, and bring structure to ambiguity
Excellent written and verbal communication, and the judgment to calibrate between an executive conversation and a working session
Willingness to travel approximately 25% and to be based in a major metro. New York preferred

ashby:reacher:eed17ee2-5827-45a6-9914-8b.summary:
Reacher is the AI-powered social commerce platform for brands and creators. We started on TikTok Shop, where we’re an official partner, and we now also build for Meta, YouTube Shopping, Amazon, and Shopify, so brands can run their creator and affiliate programs on every channel from one place. More than 2,000 brands use Reacher Pro to find creators, run outreach, and manage their programs end to end. Reacher Plus is our AI-native managed service, and the Reacher Creator app helps thousands of creators earn more, paying out over $500K to creators every month.

We’re backed by Y Combinator and Steve Huffman (CEO of Reddit), have years of runway, and have tripled revenue in the last year. Our team of 35 works across the US, Europe, and Asia. It’s a small team growing fast, so the work you do here has a real impact on brands and creators from day one.

sections.title: About the role
paras: We're hiring a Product Manager to own product work across Reacher. Reacher is an AI-powered TikTok Shop affiliate platform used by thousands of brands. We build Pro software for creator discovery, outreach, and affiliate CRM; Reacher Plus, our AI-native managed agency; and the Creator Network app. You'll talk to customers, turn what you hear into a clear plan, and ship with engineering. You'll report to Yuyin, our Head of Product. This is a hands-on role at a small company, so you will write the specs and stay close to the work until it ships.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Talk to brands, agencies, and creators to understand what is working and what is getting in their way
Turn customer feedback into a clear product plan and a backlog the team can actually ship
Write tight specs and work with engineering to get features into production
Own products end to end across Pro, Reacher Plus, and the Creator app, as priorities require
Define success with simple metrics and use them to decide what to build next
Work closely with Yuyin, engineering, and go-to-market so launches land cleanly

sections.title: What you bring
bullets: Experience as a product manager at a startup or growth-stage company, ideally in B2B software
You've taken features from a customer conversation to a shipped product
You write clearly and can explain tradeoffs without extra process
Comfort talking to customers and pushing back when a request is the wrong problem to solve
Comfort working fast in a startup and doing the work yourself

bullets: Familiarity with TikTok Shop, social commerce, or creator marketing
Experience with AI or automation products
You've worked closely with design and engineering on a small team

ashby:revenuecat:e2358195-187c-4d7e-8081.summary:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile.

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $18B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 180+ people across 30+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance.

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that…

sections.title: The Role
paras: As Senior Product Manager, User Acquisition, you'll explore an important extension of how RevenueCat helps developers grow: helping them not just monetize the users they have, but acquire more of the right users in the first place.

RevenueCat already has several footholds in user acquisition, including our Apple Ads integration and integrations across the attribution and MMP ecosystem. But we're still early in defining what a broader RevenueCat user acquisition product should become. You'll be the first dedicated product hire focused on this space, reporting directly to our product lead for Ads, with significant latitude to shape both the strategy and the products we build.

This is a zero-to-one role: you won’t inherit a predetermined roadmap. You’ll own the discovery and delivery of products that help app developers acquire users. We’re looking for someone who has identified customer problems, made difficult prioritization decisions, and partnered with engineering and design to ship products customers use. Your experience in acquisition and measurement will inform which problems we pursue and how we solve them.

sections.title: About you:
bullets: You bring relevant experience in mobile user acquisition, attribution, measurement, or advertising products. You understand how mobile acquisition teams work, the tools they rely on, and the trade-offs they face. You may have developed this expertise by building products for acquisition teams or by working directly in acquisition.
Experience building products for acquisition teams—such as attribution, measurement, advertising platforms, or acquisition analytics—is especially valuable. Hands-on campaign management is a plus.
You understand the modern mobile acquisition stack, including MMPs and attribution, Apple Ads, Meta and Google advertising products, conversion APIs, and related measurement infrastructure.

You can reason clearly about attribution, performance-marketing economics, and privacy. You understand concepts such as CAC, LTV, ROAS, optimization signals, ATT, SKAdNetwork/AdAttributionKit, consent management, and how downstream behavior should influence acquisition decisions.

You thrive in zero-to-one environments. You can take a large, ambiguous opportunity, identify the most important unanswered questions, narrow it into product bets, and find pragmatic ways to test those bets before making large investments.
You are sufficiently technical to work closely with engineering on integrations, APIs, SDKs, data flows, identity, attribution, and other technical product decisions.
You communicate clearly across different audiences and media, particularly in writing.

sections.title: In the first month, you'll:
bullets: Spend significant time with developers understanding how they acquire users today, how they evaluate acquisition performance, and where the process is painful, expensive, fragmented, or opaque.
Build a deep understanding of RevenueCat's existing acquisition-related products, integrations, data, customer research, and technical capabilities.
Build strong working relationships with engineering, design, data, go-to-market, and other product teams whose work intersects with user acquisition.
Develop a clear picture of the acquisition ecosystem, the problems RevenueCat is particularly well positioned to solve, and the biggest assumptions we still need to test.
Begin forming your own point of view on where RevenueCat could create differentiated value in user acquisition.

sections.title: Within the first 3 months, you'll:
bullets: Have narrowed the broad user acquisition opportunity into a small number of concrete product hypotheses, grounded in customer research, market understanding, and RevenueCat's unique advantages.
Have a clear recommendation for where we should focus first — and why.
Begin validating that direction through prototypes, design partners, technical exploration, lightweight product experiments, or an initial shippable bet.
Establish a learning agenda that makes the biggest risks and unanswered questions explicit, and gives us a fast path to increasing or decreasing our conviction.
Align senior stakeholders around what we're testing, what we're not pursuing yet, and what evidence would cause us to change direction.

ashby:serval:7d582aa0-45fa-415f-ba82-d7f.summary:
Serval is the AI-native enterprise service management platform that automates the work legacy IT service management tools only track. Our AI agents build the automations that power employee support, then resolve requests against them instantly—helping teams across IT, HR, finance, legal, and beyond automate work within one governed platform.

Companies including Fox, Live Nation, Notion, Ramp, and Lucid Motors run on Serval. Headquartered in San Francisco, we’ve raised $277 million from investors including Sequoia Capital, Redpoint Ventures, First Round, General Catalyst, and Elad Gil, most recently a $150 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation.

sections.title: Who We Are
paras: We’re building a team that moves quickly, takes ownership, and wants to make a meaningful impact on how the world’s largest organizations work. Come help us build what’s next for enterprise service management.

sections.title: Role Overview
paras: This is our founding Solutions Engineer: the first technical seller at Serval and the person who defines what world-class solutions architecture looks like here. You'll own the technical side of the pre-sales cycle for prospective strategic customers, sitting across the table from sophisticated IT and security buyers who test every claim we make. Your job is to earn their trust, prove the platform, and win the technical decision. Because you're first, you're not inheriting a playbook, you're writing it: partnering directly with our GTM leaders and account executives, shaping how we demo and run technical evaluations, and building the technical foundation the next ten SAs will use.

sections.title: Who You Are
bullets: A builder at heart, able to scope what matters, stand up a demo or proof-of-value yourself, and ship it.
Deeply technical and credible, the kind of person who earns the respect of CIOs, Heads of IT, and security leaders in the first meeting.
A trusted advisor by instinct, who listens for the real problem and proves value in the sales cycle rather than pitching features.
Living on the AI frontier, fluent in how agents and LLM-powered systems get deployed and governed inside the enterprise.
Comfortable in ambiguity, owning your work end-to-end, and moving without waiting to be told what to build next.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Run the technical sales motion with AEs: discovery, architecture, demos, whiteboard sessions, executive briefings, and the security review that wins technical buy-in.
Go deep on integrations with the prospect's stack, including identity providers (Okta, Entra), ITSM and ticketing, MDM, HRIS, cloud, and the SaaS apps Serval provisions against.
Translate unique technical environments, requirements, and goals into a scoped set of value-based use cases and success criteria for pilot.
Be the credible voice on security and access, fluent in guardrails, approval workflows, least-privilege and just-in-time access, audit logging, and the compliance questions security teams press on.
Execute a clean handoff to Deployment at pilot kickoff, with full technical context, then roll off the account.
Build the foundational SA toolkit from scratch: demo environments, reference architectures, evaluation frameworks, technical FAQs, and competitive positioning.
Act as the bridge between the field and product, capturing the hardest objections and feature gaps and working directly with engineering to close them.

ashby:sierra:9be563fa-0231-4e7a-a482-5ed.summary:

bullets: Join us to bring AI agents to the businesses that quietly run the economy — and help build technology that makes these essential services faster, more reliable, and more human for everyone who depends on them.

sections.title: What you'll do

bullets: Experience translating code, technical logic and user requirements to product and engineering requirements

ashby:skelar:3ddb3b0a-f683-4d2b-8925-03b.summary:
SKELAR is a venture builder — a company that builds companies. Together with founders, we create and grow global consumer businesses across EdTech, Mental Health, Petcare, FashionTech, and other industries.

Our teams build tech products that receive recognition from Product Hunt and The Webby Awards, earn thousands of positive reviews on Trustpilot, and reach millions of users worldwide. Today, products developed by SKELAR businesses are used by 10+ million people globally.

We believe that strong teams are the foundation of successful businesses. That’s why our people are our greatest value, and we create an environment where talented specialists can take on ambitious challenges, grow professionally, and make a real impact.

sections.title: What’s worth knowing about SKELAR?
paras: We have an exciting opportunity to join one of our partner companies in the Wellbeing industry . The business is building a global system of digital products designed to help people improve their relationship with themselves and enhance their everyday well-being.

As the business continues to scale globally, we are looking for a Product Manager to join their team and help drive the growth and development of our products by solving complex business challenges, working closely with cross-functional teams, and delivering real impact for our users and the company.

sections.title: What You Will Be Responsible For:
bullets: Dive deep into new business domains, quickly understanding and structuring complex problems.
Work directly with the CPO and product teams to identify growth opportunities and deliver solutions that move key business metrics.
Take ownership of hypotheses from ideation to execution, ensuring clarity, simplicity, and business value at every step.

sections.title: What We Expect From You:

You focus on results, understand business goals, and are ready to “get things done” for impact.
You’re not afraid to tackle new challenges, learn fast, and find simple, effective solutions without overcomplicating.

Can empathize with users and put yourself in their shoes to build products they’ll love.
Have experience working in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where priorities can shift quickly.

ashby:skydio:e8c33c0d-fdaa-497b-9f2c-fce.summary:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. sections.title: About Bombas:
paras: Bombas is a comfort focused premium basics brand with a mission to help those in need. The company launched in 2013, after the founders learned that socks are the #1 most requested clothing item at homeless shelters. From there, they set out to solve that problem, donating a pair of socks for every pair they sell. How do you donate a lot of socks? You sell a lot. And how do you sell a lot? You make the most comfortable socks in the history of feet. Millions of pairs sold and donated later, Bombas has continued to innovate within its mission and product, introducing new socks, as well as underwear and t-shirts, the #2 and #3 most requested clothing items at homeless shelters, all while continuing to make a positive impact on the community where we all work and live.
Click here to see what it's like to work inside the Bombas Hive!

The word Bombas is derived from the Latin word for bumblebees. Bees work together to make their hive a better place. At Bombas, we’re inspired by that. We know it’s the collective efforts of our team that keeps the Hive alive and strong - a team that is diverse and inclusive. Different perspectives strengthen our ability to make the most comfortable versions of the products people wear closest to their bodies every day and to serve the communities where we all work and live. We are committed to continuously building a Hive where all are welcomed, seen, and heard regardless of age, color, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, genetics, physical or mental ability, protected veteran status race, religion and sexual orientation. As a team, we will strive to create room for different experiences and empower all voices.

sections.title: About the Job:
paras: We are looking for an analytical, customer-obsessed team player to join our Digital Product team as our Senior Digital Product Manager – Retention & Post-Purchase , reporting directly to our Head of Digital Product. The ideal candidate has digital product management experience in the second half of the customer journey: everything after the order is placed, including order tracking, returns and exchanges, accounts, self-service support, personalization for returning customers, and the surfaces a repeat customer sees first.

This is an opportunity to own a mission from the start, leading a dedicated group of engineers and designers to turn a completed purchase into the next one. We are standing this team up now, and the post-purchase work running inside other teams today transfers to you. Your first big bet comes together with the Head of Digital Product, since we have few learnings in this space so far. After that ramp, the strategy is yours: discovery, hypotheses, and the iteration roadmap. The mandate is the customer-facing experience end to end. The platform underneath it (identity, customer and order data, internal agent tooling) sits with dedicated platform teams you partner with rather than own.

sections.title: What you’ll be responsible for:
bullets: Own the end-to-end product strategy and roadmap for post-purchase, retention, and returning-customer surfaces, including order tracking, returns and exchanges, the account experience, order history, self-service support, and personalization.

Move the team north star: sessions returning to a meaningful product interaction within 30 days of a purchase. Own the input metrics beneath it (repeat rate, account creation and login rate, self-service resolution rate, post-purchase surface engagement) and report on them.

Own personalization for returning customers. Define what a repeat session sees and the rules behind it (reorder, size and fit memory, recently purchased, replenishment timing), working from the customer and order data our platform teams expose, and prove which rules earn their place.

In this strategic leadership position, you will manage, scale, and mentor a team of Solutions Engineers driving technical pre-sales and architecture design across critical markets. Your day-to-day will involve overseeing in-depth technical feasibility studies, shaping deployment strategies for complex charging networks, and partnering closely with executive sales leadership to close high-stakes enterprise deals. You will act as a key advisor to both our largest customers and our internal engineering teams, identifying market trends and technical requirements that shape our hardware and software roadmaps. sections.title: From the job description

Neighborhood Keeper enables anonymous, machine-speed sharing of extended operational technology (xOT) threat intelligence, spanning traditional OT and ICS control systems, industrial IoT devices, and the enterprise-connected infrastructure that influences physical operations, across industries and geographic regions, empowering critical infrastructure operators, from small utilities and municipalities to large industrial enterprises, to defend their environments collectively. You will work closely with the product team, leadership, internal stakeholders, customers, and trusted advisor partners, including government agencies and ISACs, to drive an effective product roadmap through discovery, prioritization, definition, and execution for Neighborhood Keeper.
bullets: Own and evolve the product vision and strategy for Neighborhood Keeper, Dragos's collective defense platform that shares anonymized xOT threat intelligence at machine-speed across industries, sectors, and regions.
Translate participant feedback, government partner input, and the evolving xOT threat landscape into a clear quarter-over-quarter Neighborhood Keeper roadmap.

Drive development of core Neighborhood Keeper capabilities, including anonymized telemetry query federation, community-wide threat visibility, Knowledge Pack distribution, and Trusted Insight Alert delivery.

Define and evolve the platform's privacy and anonymization architecture, including federated query design, double anonymization approaches, and participant identity protection, in close partnership with Engineering and legal and policy stakeholders.

At the Staff level, your scope extends beyond a single group. Your direction will inform the broader Infrastructure Platforms direction, you’ll make the investment case for unified deployment capabilities, and you’ll be a recognized authority, inside and outside GitLab, on multi-tenant and cellular SaaS architecture. In your first year, you’ll partner closely with engineering and product peers to define requirements, drive alignment, and move this work from concept into a deployment model teams can build on, while coaching fellow product managers as they pick up work from the shared pool.

sections.title: What you’ll do

Set quarterly and annual plans for tenant portability and platform unification, breaking large epics into issues and minimal valuable changes (MVCs) and practicing iteration across multiple groups.
Define requirements for our unified deployment platform, including the capabilities needed before tenants can be hosted in a unified deployment unit.
Partner closely with engineering counterparts and highly technical teams to turn infrastructure constraints and platform needs into clear product direction.

Collaborate with product peers across the platforms organization, including teams working on GitLab.com and adjacent infrastructure areas, and manage with influence to align work that spans more than one group.

Engage with internal and external customers to understand needs related to isolation, regional deployment, compliance, and operational readiness, using qualitative interviews to find patterns and sharpen problem statements.
Build business cases for investment in tenant scale and unified deployment, including build, buy, and partner options, the cost of isolation, regionality, and compliance, and the expected benefits.

Facilitate tradeoff discussions around scalability, tenant encapsulation, deployment consistency, and platform unification, and escalate cleanly to the right level of leadership when decisions or progress are blocked.

greenhouse:mercury:6098827004.summary: In the days after the 1906 earthquake and fire destroyed most of San Francisco, the city's banks stayed shut, their vaults too hot to open for weeks. Amadeo Giannini, who ran the small Bank of Italy, did the opposite. He set up a makeshift desk on the wharf, a plank laid across two barrels, and began lending. Most of his customers were shopkeepers, fishermen, and tradespeople who had lost everything, including any papers proving who they were. So Giannini lent on a signature and a handshake, betting on the people in front of him. Those loans helped rebuild the city block by block, and, the story goes, every one of them was paid back.

sections.title: About Scopely
paras: Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.

Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.

Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.

Our portfolio of gut-directed products is developed in collaboration with leading scientists and backed by human clinical research. Beyond the body, SeedLabs —our environmental research division—advances microbial solutions that restore biodiversity and support ecosystems…

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Seed is seeking a Senior Product Manager (Member Product), reporting to the VP, Digital Product + Ecommerce, to own the end-to-end post-purchase member experience—from the moment a member converts through ongoing retention, cross-sell, and deepening engagement. As Seed expands into retail, Amazon, and new marketplaces, the member experience becomes the connective tissue across channels; this role defines what that experience should become and proves it in the market through rapid experimentation.

sections.title: What You’ll Do (Essential Functions)
bullets: Own the end-to-end post-purchase member experience strategy, defining what Seed’s member journey should look and feel like, how it evolves, and what to build to make it real.
Translate Seed’s science, brand, and retention goals into a clear product vision that earns sustained member engagement.
Design and run short-cycle experiments that test strategic hypotheses about member behavior and generate real signal.
Define the membership value architecture, grounded in what members want and what moves retention.
Own the content delivery strategy that makes science education a retention driver, moving toward dynamic, personalized surfacing.
Partner with Product Design to set the creative and strategic direction for member-facing experiences, including the member homepage and subscription management.
Collaborate with Growth Product on the funnel-to-member handoff and cross-sell positioning within the member journey.
Contribute to multi-category expansion by understanding how multi-product subscription behaviors develop and where the experience must evolve.

sections.title: What Success Looks Like
bullets: Within 6 months: a clear, defensible member experience strategy, and at least two experiments launched and generating real signal.
Within 12 months: measurable improvement in member retention and multi-product adoption, driven by experience depth rather than discounting.
Within 12 months: a recommendation on membership tier architecture backed by in-market data.
Within 12 months: a content delivery system that has moved beyond static logic toward dynamic, personalized surfacing.

sections.title: Who You Are (Required)
bullets: 7+ years of product management experience, with significant depth in post-purchase, member, subscriber, or retention-focused product work.
Experience defining experience strategy from ambiguity—articulating what a product should become and building conviction around that vision.
A track record of leading cross-functional teams (design, engineering, brand, marketing) by setting strategic direction, not only managing delivery.
Product experience in DTC ecommerce, including subscription or membership businesses at meaningful scale, and an understanding of retention as an experience problem.
Analytical fluency, including cohort analysis, LTV modeling, and experiment design.
Experience with experimentation-driven product development: rapid prototyping, hypothesis-driven testing, and short-cycle iteration.
Experience writing product strategy documents, PRDs, and experiment briefs, and proficiency with product analytics tools.
Clear, structured communication that makes complex strategy understandable to senior stakeholders and cross-functional partners.

greenhouse:sentinellabs:8204547003.summary: At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

sections.title: What Are We Looking For?
paras: We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Deployment Customer Success Manager, Strategic Accounts, you will be tasked with leading the customer-side success of SentinelOne's largest and most complex partner-delivered implementations, as our expanded global relationship with strategic partners brings together SentinelOne's AI-powered security platform and our partners' expertise in managed detection and response, managed SIEM, and incident response. You will coordinate executive stakeholders, technical prerequisites, cross-functional dependencies, regulatory or data residency constraints where applicable, and formal acceptance, helping ensure clear customer ownership, technical quality, and measurable results as partner-delivered services grow. This is a senior orchestration role that connects commercial promises, technical scope, and the real-life conditions required for a deployment to succeed.

sections.title: What Will You Do?
bullets: Own strategic deployment success plans, executive governance, success criteria, and milestone alignment across high-complexity accounts.
Establish customer and internal stakeholder maps, decision rights, escalation pathways, and readiness checkpoints.
Validate POV exit criteria, solution design, SOW scope, and implementation assumptions before work begins.
Collaborate with partner delivery leadership to address schedule risk, scope drift, customer dependencies, and technical escalations.
Coordinate data sovereignty, regulatory, security, change-management, and enterprise architecture requirements when applicable to each customer.
Facilitate executive steering updates and provide transparent, action-oriented communication on delivery health.
Engage SentinelOne architects, Product, Support, and customer success leaders to unblock high-risk implementation issues.
Verify acceptance evidence, production readiness, first value, and handoff into ongoing technical/customer success.

sections.title: What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?
bullets: 5 or more years in enterprise customer success, complex implementation governance, professional-services program coordination, or technical account management.
A successful track record with strategic enterprise deployments involving multiple technical and executive stakeholders.
A working understanding of EDR/XDR, SIEM, security architecture, integrations, or enterprise cybersecurity operations.
The ability to navigate procurement, regulatory, security assurance, and change-control requirements without overstating technical authority.
Strong executive presence, written reporting, negotiation, and escalation leadership.
Experience partnering with systems integrators or external technical service organizations.
Disciplined control of project scope, customer readiness, decisions, acceptance, and risk registers.
Familiarity with AI SIEM, enterprise endpoint migrations, or AI runtime security implementations.

sections.title: Why SentinelOne?
paras: AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.
We invest in our Sentinels with comprehensive, competitive benefits designed to support you and your family:

sections.title: About ShipHawk
paras: ShipHawk is on a mission to become the operating system for modern commerce operations. Our advanced Transportation Management System (TMS) and Warehouse Management System (WMS) help retailers, wholesalers, and ecommerce companies simplify complex fulfillment operations, reduce costs, and deliver exceptional customer experiences.
We bring enterprise-level shipping and warehouse capabilities to mid-market businesses, empowering them to compete with the largest companies in the world.
As we continue to innovate, we're embedding AI, automation, and data intelligence into our platform to make fulfillment operations smarter, faster, and increasingly autonomous.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We are seeking an experienced and highly motivated Platform Product Manager to own the strategy, roadmap, and execution of ShipHawk's core Transportation Management System (TMS) and shared platform capabilities.

In this role, you'll drive innovation across critical shipping workflows, including rate shopping, carrier selection, shipment execution, and documentation, while helping shape the future of AI-powered automation across our TMS and WMS products.
You'll collaborate closely with Engineering, Product, Sales, Customer Success, and other cross-functional teams to deliver scalable solutions that create measurable value for our customers.

sections.title: Product Strategy & Roadmap
bullets: Own and execute the product strategy and roadmap for ShipHawk's core TMS and shared platform capabilities.
Prioritize initiatives based on customer needs, business impact, market opportunities, and engineering capacity.
Conduct ongoing customer discovery to understand shipping, warehouse, and operational challenges.
Monitor industry trends, emerging technologies, and competitive developments to identify opportunities for differentiation.
Define clear product success metrics and measure performance following launch.

sections.title: AI & Platform Innovation
bullets: Help define and execute ShipHawk's AI strategy across TMS and WMS, identifying opportunities to automate manual workflows and improve decision-making.
Partner with Engineering to develop scalable platform foundations, including shared data models, APIs, and reliable shipment and event data.
Evaluate opportunities to build, buy, or partner on AI capabilities, considering customer value, cost, scalability, and risk.
Collaborate with other Product Managers to deliver consistent, integrated capabilities across ShipHawk's platform.
Explore emerging AI technologies, including agentic workflows and intelligent automation, to improve customer productivity.

greenhouse:showpad:8041792.summary:
Showpad is building a Revenue Intelligence engine that transforms raw signals—CRM data, email threads, transcripts, and content engagement—into prescriptive AI guidance. We are looking for a technical Product Manager to own the unified data intelligence layer that powers this engine.

You will define how we capture and model data, and critically, determine the best retrieval and inference strategies (Search, RAG, Knowledge Graphs, or Vector Similarity) for every use case.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Data Modeling & Architecture : Define the canonical model for entities (deals, contacts, skills) and establish the retrieval strategy—choosing between keyword, dense vector, hybrid, or graph traversal based on latency and accuracy.

Search & RAG Ownership : Own the end-to-end RAG pipeline (chunking, embeddings, indexing). Write technical specs for retrieval layers in Meeting Prep and Roleplay AI, and define evaluation metrics (Recall@k, MRR).
Revenue Intelligence Roadmap : Drive the vision from "trusted foundation" to "prescriptive AI." Own the product logic for Deal Health and Winning Behavior models.
Platform Enablement : Act as the internal PM champion for the data platform, providing semantic primitives, event taxonomies, and data contracts to other product squads.
Discovery & Strategy : Conduct deep customer discovery and stay ahead of LLM/Search trends, translating fuzzy business questions into scoped ML problems.

sections.title: Required Skills
bullets: 5+ years in PM: at least 2 years specifically owning data platforms, search, analytics, or ML products.
Retrieval Expertise: Hands-on experience shipping RAG pipelines or search systems. You understand the trade-offs between BM25, vector search, and reranking.
Data Technicality : Fluency with Datalake architectures (Delta Lake, BigQuery, etc.) and strong entity-relationship modeling skills.
ML Fluency : Ability to define features, label designs, and evaluation metrics. You can review a technical design doc alongside engineers.
Skilled at translating complex technical infrastructure into clear business value for executive stakeholders.
Experience in B2B SaaS, CRM, or Sales Enablement.
Knowledge of graph databases (Neo4j, Neptune).
Prior background as a Data Engineer or Scientist.
